answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments bind each autonomous agent to a Merkle-rooted history while a verifiable delay function imposes a deterministic time-lock on identity minting, rendering Sybil cloning costly. Staking collateral of 10 ETH per credential is slashed by 90 percent on any double-registration proof, yielding an expected attacker utility of -8.5 ETH and establishing a strict Nash equilibrium. The protocol kernel leverages a VRF-based leader sortition seeded by an ivory beacon and a willow accumulator compresses state to O(log n) verification.
